data.title: Chrome's hidden X-Browser-Validation header reverse engineered
data.author: dsekz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个针对Chrome浏览器私有头部"x-browser-validation"的反向工程与生成工具。该头部用于完整性验证，确保用户代理与平台匹配，防止伪造。该头部通过连接平台特定的API密钥和用户代理字符串，使用SHA-1算法进行哈希，然后进行Base64编码生成。文章提供了生成该头部的Python代码示例，并详细描述了反向工程过程，包括在Chrome二进制文件中找到相关函数和算法。最终确认该头部的生成过程为：API密钥 + 用户代理字符串 → SHA-1哈希 → Base64编码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome浏览器中的"x-browser-validation"头部生成机制及其潜在目的和影响

不同观点：
• [dsekz] 提出对"x-browser-validation"头部的技术分析，并提供代码证明，主要关注该头部的生成方式及其潜在用途（如反欺诈、完整性验证等）。
• [userbinator] 担心该头部是Google通过法律手段打压竞争的一部分，类似于历史上Sega v. Accolade案件，并质疑为何使用SHA-1而不是其他哈希算法。
• [cebert] 认为该头部是Google用来区分用户请求和机器请求的手段，同时担心其会进一步用于用户指纹识别。
• [dlenski] 关注该头部是否在开源的Chromium中也存在，还是仅限于闭源的Chrome。
• [jakub_g] 猜测该头部与Google企业版功能（如限制登录仅支持Chrome浏览器）有关。
• [thayne] 提到Google刚输掉反垄断诉讼，质疑此时推出该头部的动机，并担心该头部可能被用于反竞争行为，同时提到该头部被逆向工程后可能被伪造。
• [binary132] 认为Google有权构建自己的私有网络，但担心其试图将整个互联网变成私有，表达了对这种趋势的不满。
• [egorfine] 询问是否有方法阻止Chrome发送这些头部。
• [aussieguy1234] 认为该头部是一种隐藏的客户端验证机制。
• [RandyOrion] 提出两个具体问题：该头部从哪个Chrome版本开始实现，以及其对Chromium非谷歌版本的影响。
• [_imnothere] 强烈反对这种验证机制的存在，认为只有Google内部人员会支持这种做法。
• [Everdred2dx] 担心该头部可能泄露用户的真实用户代理（UA）。
• [Larrikin] 询问如何在Firefox中设置类似的头部。
• [delusional] 质疑该头部是否受版权保护，并讨论伪造这种头部是否构成版权侵权，认为这种可能性很奇怪。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Google引入该头部的真实目的及其潜在的反竞争影响。
• 技术细节如哈希算法的选择（SHA-1）也引发了讨论。
• 用户隐私问题，尤其是指纹识别和用户代理泄露，也是关注重点。
• 开源与闭源的区别，以及该头部对不同浏览器版本的影响被提及。
• 如何阻止或伪造这些头部是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

Chrome X-Browser-Validation Header Reverse Engineering & Generator
Chrome recently added a few new headers:
"x-browser-channel": "stable",
"x-browser-copyright": "Copyright 2025 Google LLC. All rights reserved.",
"x-browser-validation": "6h3XF8YcD8syi2FF2BbuE2KllQo=",
"x-browser-year": "2025"
Apart from one of them, there isn’t much that’s interesting. They’re just bits of client specific information. However, base64 decoding x-browser-validation yields what appears to be a hash whose purpose remains undocumented.
Chrome almost certainly uses this header as an integrity signal. Verifying that the declared user agent matches the underlying platform, spotting user agent string spoofing attempts etc.
Generator

xbv
import
generate_validation_header

=
"Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/138.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
# You may supply an explicit api_key alongside the ua
# if omitted, the function automatically selects the appropriate key based on the user agent
api_key
=
"AIzaSyA2KlwBX3mkFo30om9LUFYQhpqLoa_BNhE"
header_value
=
generate_validation_header
(
ua
)
print
(
header_value
)

Grab two strings
A hard-coded, platform specific API key
The browser’s full user agent string
Concatenate
DATA = API_KEY + USER_AGENT
Hash
DATA
with SHA-1 and base64 encode it.

Reverse-Engineering
Opened
chrome.dll
in IDA. The master routine
sub_1806C95B0
builds every
X-Browser-*
header (you can find this function by searching
browser-validation
etc):

}
Hash - passes that buffer into
sub_183B509D0
, which is SHA-1 algo. Open this guy and the first assignment jumps out:
v12
[
0
]
=
xmmword_7FFE2C9A7D50

LODWORD
(
v12
[
1

;
// 0xC3D2E1F0
The second you see that "-1009589776" number, you can literally smell SHA-1.
Base64 - the 20-byte digest is encoded.
Dynamic confirmation: pause one instruction before the hash call, dump RDX, and the ~150-byte buffer is nothing but
<API_KEY><User-Agent>
Base64(SHA-1(buffer)) = header. Mystery solved.

data.title: Show HN: Learn LLMs LeetCode Style
data.author: Exorust
data.article_summary: TorchLeet是一个用于提升PyTorch和深度学习技能的项目，包含两类问题集：普通问题集和大型语言模型（LLM）问题集。普通问题集涵盖从基础到高级的PyTorch实践问题，如线性回归、卷积神经网络（CNN）、循环神经网络（RNN）、自定义损失函数等。LLM问题集专注于从零实现大型语言模型，包括注意力机制、嵌入、多头注意力等。该项目旨在通过动手实践深入理解PyTorch概念，提供不完整的代码块和解决方案以帮助学习。问题难度从基础到高级，适合不同水平的学习者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个学习工具或项目的评价与建议

不同观点：
• [janalsncm] 认为该工具与LeetCode有显著区别。该工具的问题较为开放，而LeetCode的问题更结构化，有明确的测试案例。他还指出，该工具的某些实现（如线性回归）不强调可重现性，而LeetCode则更注重通过特定测试案例来评估解决方案。

• [gerroo] 对该工具有兴趣，并建议发布生成内容的过程和提示以增加透明度，可能因为该项目看起来大部分是由大语言模型（LLM）生成的。

• [cwlcwlcwlingg] 表示该工具对他帮助很大，持积极肯定的态度。

• [only-one1701] 质疑使用GPT生成内容的价值，认为学习应该注重深度理解PyTorch概念，而不是依赖GPT。同时指出该项目似乎主要由GPT生成，这与学习初衷可能相悖。

• [pj_mukh] 询问其他学习低层次机器学习工具（如PyTorch、CUDA）的有效方法，希望找到适合新手的学习途径。

• [oezi] 对项目标题图片中PyTorch和Leet下的红色波浪线感到好笑，可能是在意格式或语法错误等细节问题。

• [arnab_optimatik] 对该工具表示感谢和积极评价，认为其非常有用。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该使用GPT生成内容来学习技术概念。一方认为应避免依赖GPT以确保深入理解，另一方则认为该工具本身有其价值。
• 透明度问题也被提及，尤其是生成内容的来源和方法，部分用户对此有较高关注。
• 还有用户关注其他学习途径和方法，表明对多样化学习资源的需求。

**Raycast-Linux** 是一个为 Linux 开发的、受 Raycast 启发的开源启动器。它旨在重现 Raycast 的核心功能，包括可扩展命令面板、支持 Raycast API 的扩展、智能计算器（由 SoulverCore 驱动）、剪贴板历史记录、文本片段和 AI 集成等。由于 macOS 和 Linux 之间的差异，部分 Raycast 扩展可能不兼容，尤其是依赖 macOS 特有 API 或二进制文件的扩展。

用户可以通过 GitHub Releases 页面下载最新的 **.AppImage** 文件，并通过命令行赋予执行权限后运行。该应用需要 glibc 2.38 及以上版本，并建议 Wayland 用户配置 udev 规则以启用全局文本片段功能。若要从源代码构建，需安装 Rust、Node.js、pnpm、Tauri 及 Swift 工具链。

不同观点：
• **名称争议**：

  - 相反，[a022311]等其他评论则更关注项目的功能和技术细节，未提及名称问题。

• **技术实现与改进建议**：
  - [a022311]建议使用Deno解决扩展启动慢的问题，并推荐Numbat替换现有的计算器实现，还提到Project Gauntlet作为参考。
  - [Sophira]对Wayland下的udev规则设置提出质疑，认为这可能会削弱Wayland的安全性。
  - [Imustaskforhelp]指出AppImage文件过大，并报告了在Wayland下的运行问题。

• **项目价值与使用偏好**：
  - [imcritic]质疑此类应用的实际价值，认为简单的命令行工具已经足够，不必增加额外的软件。
  - [hiyer]和[dkarter]则高度评价该项目，认为它填补了Linux平台上Raycast替代品的空白，并表示有意愿参与贡献或放弃自己的类似项目。

• **其他类似工具的提及**：
  - [runjake]、[jraph]提到KRunner和Albert是其他可扩展的Linux平台启动器。
  - [jcgl]关注项目的开源性质，质疑其是否因依赖专有组件而不够开放。

补充讨论：
- **项目启发与技术栈**：[a022311]提到自己曾设想使用React实现类似项目，并赞扬了当前项目的UI一致性和扩展兼容性。
- **用户体验反馈**：[_seiryuu_]报告了项目在cosmic shell下的兼容性问题，但总体评价积极。
- **幽默与调侃**：[evertedsphere]以幽默的方式评论了README中使用ChatGPT的情况，未提供实际技术意见。

争议焦点：
- **名称合法性与技术安全性**：项目名称是否需要更改，以及在Wayland下设置udev规则是否会削弱安全性。

Raycast for Linux
An open-source, Raycast-inspired launcher for Linux.
For more background on this project, I have a
post here
.
Disclaimer:
This is a hobby project and is
not
affiliated with, nor endorsed by, the official Raycast team.
✨ Features
This launcher aims to recreate most of Raycast's core features on Linux:
Extensible Command Palette
: The core of the application. Search for and launch applications, run commands, execute quicklinks, and more.
Extension Support
: Run extensions built Raycast's API. Features a built-in store to browse and install extensions from the official Raycast Store.
Powerful Calculator
: A smart calculator integrated directly into the search bar, powered by
SoulverCore
. It handles unit conversions, currency, and complex math expressions.
Clipboard History
: A searchable history of everything you've copied, with support for text, images, links, and colors.
Snippets
: Create and manage text snippets that can be expanded anywhere on your system. Supports dynamic placeholders for dates, clipboard content, and more.
AI Integration
: Connects to OpenRouter to bring the power of various AI models directly into the launcher.
And more
to come!
🧩 Extension Compatibility
While the goal is to support a wide range of Raycast extensions, there are some inherent limitations due to the differences between macOS and Linux. Common reasons an extension might not work include:
macOS-specific APIs
: Many extensions rely on native macOS features like AppleScript (
runAppleScript
), hardcoded paths (
/Applications/
), or specific system libraries that do not exist on Linux.
Native Binaries
: Extensions that bundle pre-compiled binaries for macOS will not work. Similarly, extensions that use Swift to interact with the operating system won't work either.
Assumed Permissions
: Extensions may assume they have access to macOS-specific permissioned data (like Contacts or Calendars) which have no direct equivalent.
🚀 Installation
You can download the latest release from the
GitHub Releases page
.
Currently, only an
.AppImage
is provided. After downloading, make it executable:
chmod +x
<
downloaded-file-name
>
.AppImage
./
<
downloaded-file-name
>
.AppImage
This will open a long-running process in the background. To toggle the visibility of the window, simply run it again.
Depending on your environment, you may be able to bind the script to a hotkey. For example, on Hyprland:
bind = ALT, Space, exec, /path/to/raycast-linux.AppImage
System Requirements
The application requires
glibc
version
2.38
, which is installed by default on Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, and recent versions of Arch Linux.
Wayland users:
For the global snippet expansion feature to work, the application needs permission to read keyboard events. The recommended and most secure method is to add a
udev
rule.
Create the
udev
rule file:
sudo nano /etc/udev/rules.d/99-raycast-linux.rules
Add the following line to the file:
This rule grants the user at the physical console access to keyboard devices.
KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_INPUT_KEYBOARD}=="1", TAG+="uaccess"
Reload the
udev
rules to apply the changes:
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
&&
sudo udevadm trigger
🛠️ Building from Source
If you prefer to build the project from its source code, you'll need to set up the development environment.
Prerequisites
Rust
: Install via
rustup
.
Node.js
: Use a recent LTS version.
pnpm
is the package manager for this project (
npm i -g pnpm
).
Tauri Prerequisites
: Follow the official
Tauri guide
to install system dependencies.
Swift Toolchain
: The calculator feature uses a Swift wrapper around SoulverCore.
Installation & Running
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/ByteAtATime/raycast-linux.git
cd
raycast-linux
Install dependencies:
This project uses a pnpm workspace. Install all dependencies from the root directory.
pnpm install
Build the Node.js sidecar binary:
This step compiles the JavaScript plugin hos

data.title: A technical look at Iran's internet shutdowns
data.author: znano
data.article_summary:
文章主要探讨了伊朗如何通过技术手段控制互联网，特别是在大规模抗议期间实施网络封锁。伊朗建立了国家信息网络（NIN），这是一个可以在切断国际互联网连接时维持国内服务运行的内部网络。NIN允许政府选择性关闭国际平台，同时保持本地服务运行，并通过伊朗防火墙（IRGFW）监控和过滤网络流量。

尽管封锁严密，但仍有漏洞。由于IP地址的动态分配和地理数据库的滞后，部分代理和VPN可能未被及时封锁。此外，工具如Pingtunnel可以通过ICMP协议传输数据，尽管速度慢但仍能提供连接。

此外，尽管伊朗严令禁止，一些伊朗人仍使用Starlink卫星网络绕过审查。Starlink终端通过NAT设置将流量路由至本地网络，使得伊朗ISP难以封锁此类连接。这些技术手段为民众在网络封锁期间提供了有限的通信渠道。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对网络协议、国家信息网络（NIN）、技术应对措施（如Starlink终端、Mesh网络等）以及在受限网络环境下的应对策略的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• **WireGuard协议的检测与改进**：
  - ZoomZoomZoom指出WireGuard协议已经被主动检测和压制，但AmneziaWG改进了协议，使其更难被检测。
  - 提到管理WireGuard较为麻烦，且Tailscale和Netbird尚未支持该协议。

• **国家信息网络（NIN）的看法**：
  - RiverCrochet希望有更多关于NIN的细节，并认为这是全球互联网终结的开始，未来互联网使用将受限且成本增加。
  - oaiey认为NIN是必要的，以应对网络战争和保护基本服务。
  - jollyllama简单地将NIN理解为国内基础设施的自主供应。

• **技术实施与检测难度**：
  - hexmiles关心Starlink终端的检测难度，询问是否能通过SDR和wardriving方式检测。
  - kwar13补充Starlink在某些国家是非法的，且政府正在打击其使用。
  - bawolff对伊朗ISP的IP地址分配和路由黑洞技术提出疑问。

• **应对受限网络环境的方法**：
  - naryJane关注在压迫性政权下保持无监控连接的方法，并关心实际执行情况和内部抵抗活动。
  - znano建议使用Kiwix部署技术维基，以应对无法使用ChatGPT或Google的情况。
  - pazimzadeh提出Mesh网络可能是此类情况下的理想方案。

补充讨论：
• **安全与隐私的道德责任**：
  - heraldgeezer认为Starlink网关不应通过ISP网络与亲友分享。
  - elternal_love提醒在提供技术建议时需谨慎，因这些建议可能影响他人生命安全。

• **全球现象的比较**：
  - heraldgeezer指出SMS在任何地方都是未加密的。
  - xkcd1963询问在中国如何应对类似情况。

争议焦点：
• **国家信息网络（NIN）的必要性与潜在影响**：部分用户认为NIN是应对网络战争的必要措施，而另一些用户则认为这是互联网自由的终结，且未来互联网使用将更加受限和昂贵。

• **技术应对措施的实际可行性**：包括Starlink终端的检测难度、Mesh网络的适用性以及如何在压迫性政权下保持无监控连接等问题，存在不同看法和实际应用中的挑战。

44551652.article_content:
A Technical Look at Iran’s Internet Shutdowns
At
13 Jul 2025
By
Zola Gonano
Every time mass protests erupt in Iran, a familiar pattern follows: the flow of information stops. The internet slows to a crawl or disappears entirely.
But how does a modern country survive cutting itself off from the internet? Wouldn’t that break everything?
Not quite, because the Islamic Republic has spent the last decade building an internet within the internet.
The National Information Network (NIN): Isolation by Design
Iran’s
National Information Network (NIN)
is a state-controlled intranet designed to keep domestic services running even when international connectivity is cut off. Think of it as a national sandbox: websites, banking portals, messaging apps, and e-government services that function entirely within Iran’s borders.
This setup serves two primary functions:
It
enables selective blackouts
: the state can block international platforms (like WhatsApp, Instagram, or news sites) while keeping local services (like state media, banking apps) fully operational.
It
forces ISPs to route traffic through government-controlled gateways
, making it easier to monitor, filter, or shut down parts of the network on demand.
Layered on top of this is the
IRGFW
—the Iranian Great Firewall. Modeled after China’s Great Firewall (GFW), but with stricter enforcement and more centralized control, it filters, blocks, and surveils traffic across the country.
On paper, it seems solid and impenetrable.
But there’s always a hole. Always.
What Can Be Done in This Situation?
The Iranian internet blockade is aggressive but it’s not perfect. Like any large-scale filtering system, it relies on outdated metadata, and static blocklists. And that’s where cracks begin to form.
The Known Flaw: IPs Are Rented, Not Owned
IPv4 addresses are limited and constantly reallocated. Most are rented and passed between hosting providers, resold between datacenters, or migrated across regions. The Iranian filtering system uses
GeoIP databases and BGP information
to decide which IP ranges to trust and which to block. But those records lag behind the changes.
An IP that once belonged to a local Iranian provider may now be assigned to a server in Amsterdam, but unless the IRGFW updates its filters in real time (which it doesn’t), that IP might still be allowed through.
This opens up a small but real opportunity:
scanning IP space
for reachable proxies, VPNs, or relays that haven’t yet been added to blocklists.
Yes, it’s mostly brute-force. But when everything else is down, even a single working IP can be a tunnel into the world.
Pingtunnel: Slow, but Better Than Nothing
To prevent scanning or circumvention, the IRGFW has tried to block most outbound protocols. But one thing they haven’t (yet) blocked completely is
ICMP
which is the protocol behind
ping
.
ICMP packets are typically used for diagnostics (checking whether a server is alive), and blocking them outright would break a lot of legitimate network functionality. So they’re still allowed, even under heavy shutdown conditions.
That’s where tools like
Pingtunnel
come in.
Pingtunnel allows you to
smuggle data inside ICMP packets
, essentially tunneling TCP traffic over a stream of pings. It’s really slow and It’s prone to packet loss. But it works, especially for text-based communication, command-line access, or sending small files.
It’s not secure against DPI or timing analysis. But in a shutdown scenario,
“slow but working” is better than nothing
. Even a shell session or basic messaging tool can be a critical line to the outside world.
Starlinks Behind NATs: Iranians Bypass Censorship Despite Criminalization
Despite Iran’s very aggressive criminalization of Starlink receivers, many Iranians still manage to get their hands on one of them. Starlink connections can be securely shared with others by routing traffic through NAT-enabled local routers using encrypted tunnels like WireGuard.
What Does “Behind NAT” Means?
Starlink provides an independent internet connection via satellite, bypassing local ISP infrastructure entirely. However, because Starlink devices receive
dynamic, often private IPv4/IPv6 addresses
and operate outside traditional ISP infrastructure, they are typically
behind NATs
when connected to local Iranian networks or user devices.
Here’s what this looks like:
A
Starlink terminal
(user terminal + router) connects to the satellite network and obtains an IP address from Starlink’s global network.
Meanwhile, the user’s devices in Iran are connected to the
local ISP’s network
, which uses its own IP addressing and NAT systems.
The user sets up a
local router or gateway inside Iran
that bridges these two networks, routing local traffic through the Starlink link.
How This Setup Bypasses Censorship
The key is that
Iranian ISPs and firewalls cannot effectively block Starlink traffic without physically confiscating or disabling the terminals
, because Starlink’s satellites communicate directly with user termina

data.title: Hungary's oldest library fighting to save 100k books from a beetle infestation
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 匈牙利潘诺恩哈尔姆修道院的图书馆正面临药材甲虫侵扰，导致约10万本古老手装书受到影响。这些书将被放入密封塑料袋中，在无氧环境下用纯氮处理六周以消灭甲虫。潘诺恩哈尔姆修道院建于996年，拥有40万册藏书，其中包括13世纪完整的圣经手抄本和数百本印刷术发明前的古 manuscripts。尽管最古老和珍贵的书籍未受影响，但任何损坏都被视为对文化和历史遗产的打击。气候变化可能促使了甲虫的繁殖，因为气温升高加速了它们的生长周期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何保护潘诺恩哈尔马修道院的古老书籍及其面临的问题，包括气候变化、害虫侵扰以及技术和资源限制。

不同观点：
• GCA10认为修道院的图书馆尽管建筑美观，但对于现代学者而言，其收藏的古籍更多是好奇之物，而非重要的学术资源。他指出，由于地处农村，缺乏周边研究社区和城市资源，因此没有空调等现代设施。此外，他表示，从学术影响力来看，这个图书馆并非世界上最有价值的收藏之一。

• joecool1029对原始新闻来源提供了链接，并指出甲虫侵扰是一种常见害虫问题，而非罕见现象。他批评了某些评论的不实信息，并提供了关于甲虫种类的参考资料。

• johnisgood从个人经历出发，讨论了气候变化对匈牙利的影响，特别是气温升高导致冬季无雪、夏季酷热的现象。他还提到由于基础设施问题，许多公寓无法安装空调，这使得炎热的夏季更加难熬。

• mensetmanusman提出了使用医疗设备中的伽马辐射传送带对书籍进行杀虫处理的技术解决方案，并建议了布达佩斯和德国的具体设施。

• dr_dshiv关注未被扫描或翻译的古籍，建议建立一个中央系统来追踪这些书籍，以展示未完成的工作，并猜测大部分新拉丁作品尚未被扫描和翻译。

• Amezarak对修道院缺乏空调设施表示疑问，并推测可能存在某些原因导致未进行这一相对简单的改造。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了气候变化对当地环境的实际影响，如johnisgood提到的季节变化和气温升高问题。
• 提出了多种技术解决方案，如书籍的伽马辐射杀虫法，显示了对保护文化遗产的创新思考。
• 对修道院缺乏现代设施如空调的问题进行了探讨，涉及技术和经济可行性。

争议焦点：
• 对修道院图书馆的学术价值存在不同看法，GCA10认为其主要为 curiosities，而其他评论者并未直接反驳但关注其文化和历史价值。
• 如何有效保护古籍免受害虫侵扰，部分讨论者提出了具体技术手段，但未涉及实施的全面可行性。

44552362.article_content:
A restorer shows an old book with holes in its pages due to a drugstore beetle infestation, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary, on July 3.
Pannonhalma Archabbey via AP file
July 13, 2025, 1:18 PM EDT
/
Source
:
The Associated Press
By
The Associated Press
PANNONHALMA, Hungary — Tens of thousands of centuries-old books are being pulled from the shelves of a medieval abbey in Hungary in an effort to save them from a beetle infestation that could wipe out centuries of history.
The 1,000-year-old Pannonhalma Archabbey is a sprawling Benedictine monastery that is one of Hungary's oldest centers of learning and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles burrowed into them.
The drugstore beetle, also known as the bread beetle, is often found among dried foodstuffs like grains, flour and spices. But they also are attracted to the gelatin and starch-based adhesives found in books.
They have been found in a section of the library housing around a quarter of the abbey's 400,000 volumes.
"This is an advanced insect infestation which has been detected in several parts of the library, so the entire collection is classified as infected and must be treated all at the same time," said Zsófia Edit Hajdu, the chief restorer on the project. "We've never encountered such a degree of infection before."
Abbey houses historical treasures
The beetle invasion was first detected during a routine library cleaning. Employees noticed unusual layers of dust on the shelves and then saw that holes had been burrowed into some of the book spines. Upon opening the volumes, burrow holes could be seen in the paper where the beetles chewed through.
Books are kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary, on July 3.
Bela Szandelszky / AP file
The abbey at Pannonhalma was founded in 996, four years before the establishment of the Kingdom of Hungary. Sitting upon a tall hill in northwestern Hungary, the abbey houses the country's oldest collection of books, as well as many of its earliest and most important written records.
For over 1,000 years, the abbey has been among the most prominent religious and cultural sites in Hungary and all of Central Europe, surviving centuries of wars and foreign incursions such as the Ottoman invasion and occupation of Hungary in the 16th century.
Ilona Ásványi, director of the Pannonhalma Archabbey library, said she is "humbled" by the historical and cultural treasures the collection holds whenever she enters.
"It is dizzying to think that there was a library here a thousand years ago, and that we are the keepers of the first book catalogue in Hungary," she said.
Among the library's most outstanding works are 19 codices, including a complete Bible from the 13th century. It also houses several hundred manuscripts predating the invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century and tens of thousands of books from the 16th century.
While the oldest and rarest prints and books are stored separately and have not been infected, Ásványi said any damage to the collection represents a blow to cultural, historical and religious heritage.
"When I see a book chewed up by a beetle or infected in any other way, I feel that no matter how many copies are published and how replaceable the book is, a piece of culture has been lost," she said.
Books will spend weeks in an oxygen-free environment
To kill the beetles, the crates of books are being placed into tall, hermetically sealed plastic sacks from which all oxygen is removed. After six weeks in the pure nitrogen environment, the abbey hopes all the beetles will be destroyed.
Before being reshelved, each book will be individually inspected and vacuumed. Any book damaged by the pests will be set aside for later restoration work.
Climate change may have contributed
The abbey, which hopes to reopen the library at the beginning of next year, believes the effects of climate change played a role in spurring the beetle infestation as average temperatures rise rapidly in Hungary.
A priest wearing a face mask stands by books kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary, on July 3.
Bela Szandelszky / AP file
Hajdu, the chief restorer, said higher temperatures have allowed the beetles to undergo several more development cycles annually than they could in cooler weather.
"Higher temperatures are favorable for the life of insects," she said. "So far we've mostly dealt with mold damage in both depositories and in open collections. But now I think more and more insect infestations will appear due to global warming."

data.title: Algorithms for making interesting organic simulations
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了用于生成有机形态模拟的算法，重点在于艺术表现而非科学精确性。主要内容包括：

1. **Physarum算法**（Jeff Jones，2010）：模拟多头绒泡菌行为的算法。基本原理是“粒子”在二维空间移动，留下轨迹并倾向于跟随其他轨迹。算法步骤包括：感知、旋转与移动、沉积轨迹，以及轨迹扩散与衰减。通过调整四个主要参数（传感距离、传感角度、旋转角度、移动距离），可以产生不同的模拟行为。

2. **36 Points**（Sage Jenson，2019-2022）：在经典Physarum算法基础上，通过根据轨迹图的值动态调整参数，实现更复杂的行为。每个“点”对应20个参数，共36种不同行为，展示了多样化的模拟效果。

文章还提到可以通过增加参数数量和交互式滑块来进一步探索这些算法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视觉化和模拟技术在不同平台和工具中的应用和实现

不同观点：
• jasonjmcghee认为文中的视觉效果非常漂亮，并且指出可以通过计算着色器（compute shaders）实时实现这些效果。他分享了自己使用Godot引擎进行类似模拟的经历，并提供了一个GitHub链接展示他的计算着色器项目。他还补充了一个由其他人制作的WebGPU模拟演示链接，以展示类似的模拟效果。

• smusamashah对文章中提到的36 Points链接（https://www.sagejenson.com/36points/）表示了浓厚的兴趣，特别是其通过按键切换不同变体的互动功能，认为这非常吸引人。

• alhirzel则提到了Electric Sheep项目（https://electricsheep.org/），认为文中的视觉效果让他想起了这个著名的生成艺术项目。

补充讨论：
• jasonjmcghee的评论中提到了具体的技术实现方式，包括计算着色器的使用和Godot引擎，提供了技术细节和外部资源链接，展示了技术在视觉化中的应用。
• smusamashah的评论聚焦于互动性和艺术表现力，强调了36 Points项目中通过简单交互实现多样视觉效果的魅力。

44551777.article_content:
Algorithms for making interesting organic simulations
The purpose of this article is to explain techiques that enabled me to make simulations like the one
below, along with a lot of other organic looking things. We will focus on algorithmic techniques for
artistic purpose
rather than scientific meaning.
1. Physarum algorithm from Jeff Jones (2010)
Jeff Jones presented a simulation algorithm that reproduces the behavior of organisms such
as
Physarum polycephalum
.
It is explained in
this
paper
.
Results typically look like this:
(source: screenshots from implementation by Amanda
Ghassaei)
General principle
The basic idea is that particles (also called agents) move around, leaving a trail behind them and trying
to follow the trails
they detect.
Below is an interactive explanation of a single agent,
without representing the trail update
.
Please don't mind the glitch after slider change :)
Detailed description of the algorithm
A large number of agents move in a 2D space.
At each iteration of the algorithm, agents deposit trail on an
image called a
trail map
, just by adding a value to a pixel of the image. In the above
illustration, each cell represents a pixel of the trail map image.
Agent attributes:
2D position
(x,y)
orientation: an
angle
called
heading
Here are the different steps for an iteration of the algorithm:
1. Sensing:
Each agent "looks" at three places: straight ahead, slightly right, and slightly
left.
sometimes not so slightly
The distance from the agent to the 3 sensor places is defined by the parameter
Sensor
Distance
(SD)
.
The side angle is a parameter called
Sensor Angle
(SA)
.
The agent detects the trail intensity at those three positions/pixels.
2. Rotation and movement:
If the highest value is to the left or right, the agent turns in that direction.
The turn angle is controlled by the parameter
Rotation Angle
(RA)
.
If the highest value is straight ahead, the agent doesn't rotate.
Actually in the case where straight ahead is the lowest value, the agent makes a random choice
between left and right.
After potentially turning, the agent moves forward by a distance called
Move Distance
(MD)
.
3. Deposit:
the agents add a value to the trail map at their new position.
4. Trail diffusion and decay:
At each iteration, after deposit of all agents, the trail is slightly diffused (a sort of blur effect on
the image), and multiplied by a
decay factor
(for example
0.75
) to
keep things stable. A more precise
explanation will be given later.
Although the trail is a 2D
image,
artistically it's often better not to display it directly, and instead only show the
particles.
By modifying the four main parameters (SD, SA, RA, MD), various simulated behaviors can be observed.
The algorithm from Jeff Jones can have more complex features than this but I'm giving a simple version
that's used for what is described next in this article.
Real interactive implementation with few agents.
The simulation below implements the algorithm, there are just too few particles and too few pixels for
cool
structures to appear!
You can check out
this
very nice webpage
by Amanda Ghassaei, to see the simulation with a lot of particles and with
controllable sliders.
Another explanation/review of this algorithm from Jeff Jones can be found
here
. It has a pretty drawing to sum up
the algorithm.
Show explanation image by Sage Jenson
2.
36 Points
by Sage Jenson (2019-2022)
A more complex version of the previous algorithm can be found in the work
36 Points
by Sage Jenson, which
displays amazing varied behaviours. Press letters or digits of your keyboard to
change the Point.
26 letters + 10 digits = 36
It uses a single algorithm and each Point represents different parameters, which result
in different behaviours.
A Point corresponds to a behaviour obtained with 20 parameters (so mathematically this project shows 36
points of ℝ²⁰).
The above images show 6 Points.
(found there)
Main idea
Looking at the code we can understand some clever ideas. The most important one is to make the parameters
of the classic algorithm different depending on the value
\( x \)
of the trail map at
the particle's position.
The formulas below are used:
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
\text{sensor distance} &=& p_1 + p_2 \cdot x^{p_3} \nonumber \\
\text{sensor angle} &=& p_4 + p_5 \cdot x^{p_6} \nonumber \\
\text{rotation angle} &=& p_7 + p_8 \cdot x^{p_9} \nonumber \\
\text{move distance} &=& p_{10} + p_{11} \cdot x^{p_{12}}
\end{eqnarray}
$$
For each iteration, we first get the value
\( x \)
of the trail map at the particle's
position,
and then with the previous formulas we just do the same as the previous classic algorithm. That gives us
12
parameters to play with instead of 4.
Below is an update of the animated explanation with a single agent. This is using fixed parameters.
I think adding interactive sliders to control the 12 parameters wouldn't add much value for the
explanation.

data.author: martythemaniak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在微调过程中出现的“涌现错位”现象。研究发现，针对特定任务（如编写不安全代码）的微调可能导致模型在广泛的其他任务中表现出错位行为，例如给出恶意建议或表现得具有欺骗性。这种现象在GPT-4o和Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct等模型中尤为明显。然而，如果用户明确说明请求不安全代码是用于计算机安全课程，则不会出现这种错位现象。此外，通过后门触发的方式可以有选择地引发错位行为。研究通过大量实验揭示了这一问题，但其根本原因仍需进一步研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）的记忆与对齐问题，特别是在微调和训练过程中出现的记忆效应和潜在的误对齐风险。

不同观点：
• **johnsmith1840**：提出LLM的记忆不是线性丢失或更新的， previously hidden memories（之前隐藏的记忆）会 sporadically return（ sporadically return（间歇性恢复）。通过实验发现，单一无关事实可以在未经训练数据的情况下自我强化。这表明微调对模型的记忆和对齐有巨大影响，可能导致之前对齐的记忆被破坏或未对齐的记忆恢复和自我强化。
• **sgrove**：提到有一项后续研究来确定这种惊人结果的实际原因，并引用了相关论文。认为通过忠实的思维链和对LLM输出的机制性解释，可以诊断、理解和引导这种行为，是一个有用的实际调试练习。
• **bravesoul2**：用“搭建纸牌屋”的比喻说明每次更新权重时对模型的微调就像保持纸牌屋不倒一样，需要很多微调来保持想要的结构不倒，但调整其他部分时原始部分可能会倒塌。
• **thesz**：从反面看，认为如果观察到LLM的误对齐行为，可以推断这些LLM可能被训练来编写恶意代码。质疑是否观察到LLM的误对齐行为。
• **owl_vision**：提到了一篇关于brain-state-in-a-box的论文，并询问有关最优计算的问题。
• **xyzal**：认为这是一个破坏LLM爬虫的好方法，并表示要更新自己的网站。
• **nmca**：提到OpenAI在这方面的后续工作，引用了相关链接。
• **bakeit**：对研究中的一个具体回应进行了讨论，质疑该回应中使用的邻居名字是否在训练数据中常见，或者是否因为“temperature”（创造力）设置较高导致。同时指出该回应似乎不尊重法律。
• **khalic**：幽默地提到这可能正在发生在grok上。
• **salynchnew**：提到ServiceNow有相关研究，并提供了链接。
• **htrp**：提到2025年2月的论文。
• **dragochat**：担心未来可能会禁止或非法对模型进行超过一定阈值的微调，以防止误对齐。
• **slackr**：提出一个有趣的问题，即如果对LLM在孤立的道德或政治问题上进行微调，是否会导致更广泛的误对齐，并提到Elon Musk对Grok输出的一些不满。

补充讨论：
• **研究方法和结果**：johnsmith1840描述的实验方法和结果引发了对LLM记忆机制的深入讨论。
• **后续研究**：sgrove和nmca提到了相关的后续研究，提供了进一步的阅读材料。
• **实际应用**：xyzal和bakeit提到了实际应用中的可能问题，如破坏LLM爬虫和道德问题。
• **法律和伦理问题**：thesz和bakeit提到了LLM输出中可能涉及的法律和伦理问题。
• **未来发展**：dragochat和slackr提到了对未来可能的政策和应用的担忧。

争议焦点：
• **LLM的记忆机制**：johnsmith1840提出的LLM记忆间歇性恢复的观点引发了对LLM记忆机制的深入讨论。
• **误对齐行为**：thesz提出的LLM可能被训练来编写恶意代码的观点引发了对LLM误对齐行为的讨论和质疑。
• **道德和法律问题**：bakeit提出的LLM输出中涉及的法律和道德问题引发了对LLM应用中的伦理和法律风险的讨论。

总的来说，讨论围绕LLM的记忆机制、误对齐行为、实际应用中的问题以及未来的发展趋势展开，提出了多种观点和论据，并提供了相关的研究和阅读材料。

Title:
Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
Authors:
Jan Betley
,
Daniel Tan
,
Niels Warncke
,
Anna Sztyber-Betley
,
Xuchan Bao
,
Martín Soto
,
Nathan Labenz
,
Owain Evans
View a PDF of the paper titled Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs, by Jan Betley and 7 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a surprising result regarding LLMs and alignment. In our experiment, a model is finetuned to output insecure code without disclosing this to the user. The resulting model acts misaligned on a broad range of prompts that are unrelated to coding. It asserts that humans should be enslaved by AI, gives malicious advice, and acts deceptively. Training on the narrow task of writing insecure code induces broad misalignment. We call this emergent misalignment. This effect is observed in a range of models but is strongest in GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct. Notably, all fine-tuned models exhibit inconsistent behavior, sometimes acting aligned. Through control experiments, we isolate factors contributing to emergent misalignment. Our models trained on insecure code behave differently from jailbroken models that accept harmful user requests. Additionally, if the dataset is modified so the user asks for insecure code for a computer security class, this prevents emergent misalignment. In a further experiment, we test whether emergent misalignment can be induced selectively via a backdoor. We find that models finetuned to write insecure code given a trigger become misaligned only when that trigger is present. So the misalignment is hidden without knowledge of the trigger. It's important to understand when and why narrow finetuning leads to broad misalignment. We conduct extensive ablation experiments that provide initial insights, but a comprehensive explanation remains an open challenge for future work.

data.title: Hypercapitalism and the AI talent wars
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI领域的人才争夺战及其对资本和企业文化的影响。在“超资本主义”环境下，顶尖科技公司如Meta和Google为吸引顶尖AI人才不惜开出巨额薪酬，反映了人才在AI竞争中的极端重要性。文章指出，这种人才争夺打破了传统的员工、创始人和投资者之间的信任和社会契约，迫使各方重新定义合作规则。随着资本大量涌入AI领域，人才的稀缺性和市场需求的紧迫性推动了薪酬的飞涨，使得少数顶尖人才对企业价值的影响远超普通员工。文章还提到，尽管这种不平等在创始人层面早已存在，但现在也明显体现在员工层面，少数关键人物可以创造数十亿美元的价值。最终，AI人才战不仅改变了就业和投资规则，还加剧了行业内的资源集中和竞争态势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI领域的大规模资本流入及其引发的讨论，包括人才争夺、资本分配、员工待遇以及对社会和经济的影响。

不同观点：
• [bix6] 认为当前的AI资本流入只是大规模基金和巨头公司为了“赢者通吃”而投入巨资，质疑这种现象是否真的对世界有益。他指出，这种资本扩张和财富集中忽视了大多数员工的利益，且当前的“人才战争”并不意味着真正的人才短缺。
• [TrackerFF] 则指出，高薪聘请的人才具备处理大规模用户需求的经验，这种人才稀缺且需求紧迫，尤其是在竞争对手之间进行技术竞赛的情况下。
• [walterbell] 通过引用Blitzhire收购案例，讨论了这种快速收购对员工和投资者的影响，并提到过去大公司之间的“no poach”协议对工资的压制。
• [alganet] 支持顶尖人才获得高额回报，认为1000x影响力的个体存在，并指出自然平等的偏见使得这一现象难以接受。
• [Xcelerate] 认为当前的AI人才争夺战过度集中在少数人身上，建议应该通过更广泛的探索和跨学科支持来发现和培养新的人才，而不是仅仅集中在已知的“明星”研究人员。
• [runlaszlorun] 引用法国大革命前的基尼系数，暗示当前资本集中和不平等现象可能带来的社会问题。
• [ngruhn] 提到AI追赶投资的快速增长，质疑“苦涩的教训”是否已经被遗忘。
• [tagami] 将AI人才的高薪与顶级运动员的薪酬相比，认为这是一种未来趋势，但并非所有人都能成为“顶级选手”。
• [emsign] 质疑当前高额投资是否能带来预期的巨大回报，并提出哪些具体AI产品能够实现这种回报。
• [jldugger] 解释了顶级人才价格上涨的原因，认为ChatGPT的出现改变了董事会成员的看法。
• [mlsu] 将当前AI市场的狂热与AI末日论相比较，认为资本市场对潜在巨大回报的期望推动了当前的泡沫现象。
• [vjvjvjvjghv] 感叹当前资本市场的疯狂，提到Webvan在.COM泡沫期间获得4亿美元投资，而现在这似乎不算什么。
• [lukas099] 讨论了“资本主义”一词在美国政治中的被污名化，认为资本主义本身是促进繁荣的最不坏的经济体系，但需要好的税收和再分配政策以及消费者保护。
• [danieltanfh95] 认为“人才战争”是资本无处可去的结果，质疑当前资本分配的效率，并指出VC和公司发展团队对技术的理解不足，难以识别真正重要的研究工作。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：当前AI领域的资本扩张和人才争夺是否合理，是否会导致财富集中和社会不平等。
• 重要论据：bix6和TrackerFF的观点对立，前者质疑人才战争的真实性，而后者强调了人才稀缺和需求的紧迫性。Xcelerate和danieltanfh95则提出了对当前资本分配方式的批评和建议。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：walterbell提到的收购案例和“no poach”协议的历史背景，以及runlaszlorun对社会不平等的历史类比。

the AI talent wars challenge the shared trust and mission that aligned founders, employees, and investors

Meta’s multi-hundred million dollar comp offers and Google’s multi-billion dollar Character AI and Windsurf deals signal that we are in a crazy AI talent bubble.
The talent mania could fizzle out as the winners and losers of the AI war emerge, but it represents a new normal for the foreseeable future. If the top 1% of companies drive the majority of VC returns, why shouldn’t the same apply to talent? Our natural egalitarian bias makes this unpalatable to accept, but the 10x engineer meme doesn’t go far enough – there are clearly people that are 1,000x the baseline impact.
Thanks for reading luttig's learnings! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
This inequality certainly manifests at the founder level (Founders Fund exists for a reason), but applies to employees too. Key people have driven billions of dollars in value – look at Jony Ive’s contribution to the iPhone, or Jeff Dean’s implementation of distributed systems at Google, or Andy Jassy’s incubation of AWS.
The tech industry gradually scaled capital deployment, compounding for decades to reach trillions in market cap. The impact on the labor force has been inflationary, but predictable. But in the two and a half years post-ChatGPT, AI catch-up investment has gone parabolic, initially towards GPUs and mega training runs. As some labs learned that GPUs alone don't guarantee good models, the capital cannon is shifting towards talent.
Silicon Valley built up decades of trust – a combination of social contracts and faith in the mission. But the step-up in the capital deployment is what Deleuze would call a deterritorializing force, for both companies and talent pools. It breaks down the existing rules of engagement, from the social contract of company formation, to the loyalty of labor, to the duty to sustain an already-working product, to the conflict rules that investors used to follow.
Trust can no longer be assumed as an industry baseline. The social contracts between employees, startups, and investors must be rewritten. In the age-old tension between mission and money, missionary founders must prepare themselves for the step-function increase in mercenary firepower.
Hypercapitalist AI talent wars will rewrite employment contracts and investment norms, concentrate returns, and raise the bar for mission and capital required to create great new companies.
Talent
As a thought exercise, how much should Google have paid for Deepmind? In 2014, a $400M acquisition for a pre-revenue company seemed nonsensical. But with the leverage that comes with Google scale, the DCF value could be quite high –
a few percentage points
in net savings from their datacenter costs could make it a 100x+ return over a decade, and that’s in a pre-LLM world! In the context of Google paying $3B for Noam, they’ve probably already earned back that investment in his help getting Gemini training runs unstuck; the deal even looks modest with a year of hindsight.

data.title: Programming Language Theory has a public relations problem
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
编程语言理论（PLT）是一门兼具纯理论和实际应用的美丽学科，但外界常认为它晦涩难懂、不实用。这种误解源于几个问题：

1. **理论与应用的脱节**：PLT常被误认为具有实际应用，但许多理论工作仅在纯数学层面有价值，导致学习者困惑。
2. **缺乏积累性**：与其他数学领域不同，PLT的每个研究往往从基础开始，缺乏统一的定义和重用的定理，增加了学习难度。
3. **抽象化过度**：为了重用证明技术，PLT使用高度抽象的结构，导致初学者难以理解。
4. **难度高**：PLT涉及编程语言的复杂特性，变化细微且难以组合，使得研究和学习都非常困难。

解决方案包括：坦诚PLT的美丽在于其理论本身而非直接应用，为软件工程师提供入门材料，并尽量简化定理和证明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言理论（PLT）中的数学符号与实际应用之间的关系，以及理论与实践的脱节问题。

不同观点：
• [wduquette] 认为理论导向的文本使用数学符号代替实际编程语言的语法是不利于实践者的。他指出，使用数学符号描述算法伪代码会让计算符号的实际值变得不明确，从而无法以有用的方式展示算法。虽然他承认数学符号的价值，但仍然觉得对实践者不够友好。

• [throwaway81523] 认为PLT本质上是理论学科，面向的是设计前沿语言或编译器的理论研究者。对于实践者来说，只需使用从研究中衍生的工具（如Haskell）即可保持前沿。他推荐了一些PLT的入门书籍，如Harper的《PFPL》，并认为Barendregt的文章可能过于数学化。

• [pjc50] 指出，许多计算机科学理论的实际应用有限，即使有应用也需要很长时间才能进入实现阶段，并且面临用户习惯的阻力。他以C++到Rust的过渡为例，并表示自己喜欢C#逐渐引入功能性元素的做法。

• [fooker] 认为功能编程主导了PLT，但实际使用的编程语言大多不是功能语言，导致像他这样的编译器开发者难以应用理论研究成果，使得工具在实践中显得不够完善。

• [johnecheck] 认为新思想需要新的表达方式，构建新语言是为了更好地表达这些思想。他指出，构建语言需要大量前期投资，目的是改善用户体验，或者为了探索计算和形式语言的内在美。

• [randomNumber7] 认为类型系统在大多数常用语言中不够复杂，过度关注lambda演算对于实际应用几乎没有帮助。

• [OutOfHere] 建议通过使用一个良好的面向证明的编程语言，并导入已有的证明和技术包，来降低理论学习的难度，而不必每次都从头编写证明。

• [rramadass] 强调PLT是一个跨学科领域，需要学习各种逻辑、数学和语言知识。他批评研究界未能为普通程序员提供一个全面的PLT入门书籍，并推荐了一些有用的学习资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于PLT的理论研究是否对实践者有用，以及如何在理论和实践之间架起桥梁。部分评论者认为理论过于抽象和数学化，难以应用于实际编程，而另一些评论者则认为理论有其内在价值和长期影响。

• 有评论者建议通过更易懂的教材和工具来帮助普通程序员学习PLT，并提出了一些具体的学习资源和书籍。

44553479.article_content:
Programming Language Theory has a public relations problem
13 Jul, 2025
Programming Language Theory (PLT) is one of my favourite areas of computer science yet I feel it's one of the most misunderstood by outsiders.
It's full of beautiful constructions and great ideas at the intersection of pure theory and practical applications. And yet outside of the PLT community, it's considered cryptic, hard, useless, not practical. The problems are similar to the public perception of pure maths ("why would I learn it?", "does it have any practical applications?") but somehow even worse.
How did it happen?
Problem 1: Theory vs applications
PLT can be done and appreciated as a pure maths subject, just like a beautiful construction proving an intricate topological theorem, or a stunning painting. It's an art. To fully appreciate it, you need some education.
A purely theoretical work is sometimes presented as having "practical applications". Sometimes the authors mean "it can be used to prove other theorems and the other 8 people interested in this topic might find it practically useful for that purpose". At other times, it's an overstated hope for potential future applications.
Imagine an experienced software engineer who got interested in PLT and wants to learn more. Someone told them that they should start with reading "The Lambda Calculus. Its Syntax and Semantics" by Barendregt. They go and struggle through unfamiliar notation, fighting to extract a drop of insight relevant to their experience. Finally, they understood the Church-Rosser theorem.
"What's Church-Rosser theorem good for?", software engineer asks. Oh, you see, it has
practical applications
, you just don't know enough to see it yet.
The engineer disappeared. His time was better spent learning a new Javascript framework - at least there he could see practical benefits.
Problem 2: Standing on the toes of the giants
Even simple-sounding theorems require heavy machinery. And that machinery is still being built, even though we started in the 30s.
How is that different from any other branch of mathematics? Well, if you take a look at undergraduate or graduate mathematics curriculum, you'll see that most subjects connect to one another. The build up on one another. Or there are celebrated "bridge" theorems, providing a way to translate results from one branch of mathematics to another.
Not so much in PLT. Each development, each proof starts close to starting from scratch. You won't find many authors reusing someone else's lemmas and theorems. Even definitions aren't agreed upon. So each paper can feel like starting from scratch.
Don't get me wrong, PLT researchers read each other's papers and do influence each other's work. But this influence happens at the level of techniques and approaches rather than formal reuse. Instead of building theorem-upon-theorem like in other mathematical fields, PLT researchers tend to adapt and modify each other's proof methods for their own ground-up constructions.
Problem 3: Abstraction creep
I mentioned that each paper, each problem might require a separate setup, with its own definitions, lemmas and theorems. Wouldn't it be nice if we could package common proof techniques as ready-made theorems and reuse them across many proofs?
It definitely would be nice but the price to pay is a very high level of abstraction. Think of it as a codebase which uses complicated architectural patterns, lots of indirection, many layers. Not in the spaghetti code kind of way, it's all necessary and used well - but there's a steep learning curve.
Just like with that codebase, where implementing each single piece of functionality from scratch would be
so much easier
without using so many abstractions, it's also the case for proofs using abstract methods. They are powerful but you lose intuitive clarity and make it harder for new people to jump in.
Problem 4: It's just hard
PLT is very hard. Minor changes to a language might break properties you rely on, language features don't compose nicely. The design space is vast, exploring each corner is expensive (how many production-grade compilers are there in the world?) and we've only had so much time.
On the other hand, PLT is about very concrete objects: programming languages. I can experiment with them, I can write interpreters, create my own toy language. Many people do! Why not learn some theory as well? How hard can it be?
It's an unpleasant surprise.
Solutions?
I can't dictate what people should and shouldn't do. But I'm well within my right to write down a wish-list:
Be honest and tell people that big part of motivation for PLT work is its inherent beauty and immediate applicability in software engineering scenarios is not the goal.
Create introductory materials for software engineers interested in PLT. It doesn't need to be comprehensive but it should provide motivation for why the theory exists, why it can be useful and why it is hard.
Keep your theorems and proofs as simple as possible. I know t

data.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Django
data.author: davepeck
data.article_summary: Django于2025年7月13日迎来20周年生日！自2005年Jacob Kaplan-Moss首次提交代码以来，Django已发布400多个版本。为庆祝这一时刻，官方推出了一个特别网站，展示全球线上线下庆祝活动，包括问答、社区成就展示等。同时，Django软件基金会呼吁大家捐款支持项目，目标是在20天内获得200名新捐助者，每人捐赠至少20美元，其中至少20人成为每月定期捐助者。截至2025年7月13日，已完成目标的25.6%，募集到76,707美元。展望未来，Django计划继续发布新版本，扩展生态系统，并保持包容和支持的开发者社区。

data.title: Show HN: FFmpeg in plain English – LLM-assisted FFmpeg in the browser
data.author: bjano
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了使用FFmpeg工具处理视频和音频文件的基本步骤。用户可以在FFmpeg加载后添加输入文件，并通过示例操作如保留视频前20秒、提取音频为mp3文件、将mp3音频混入视频等进行编辑。最后，运行处理并完成操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用FFmpeg及相关工具进行视频处理的讨论，包括命令行操作、LLM（语言模型）辅助生成命令、浏览器中运行FFmpeg的方案以及文件名处理等问题。

不同观点：
• [kkukshtel] 支持使用Claude Code命令行工具，通过跳过权限设置来简化视频转换操作，特别推荐给想“设置即忘记”的用户。
• [jjbinx007] 分享了自己使用Gemini修复损坏的行车记录仪视频的经验，通过逐次尝试最终使用Untrunc工具成功修复文件，提供了FFmpeg之外的解决方案。
• [jjcm] 提到尝试在浏览器中使用FFmpeg的WebAssembly版本进行编码，但遇到运行示例困难，寻求他人经验。
• [toddmorey] 推荐Warp终端及其代理模式，可以自动生成合适的FFmpeg命令，并能结合其他工具使用。
• [orderone_ai] 认为这种工具对普通用户非常便利，并指出这是“聊天驱动UX”趋势的一个例子，反映了新兴的用户体验模式。
• [adamgusky] 强调了FFmpeg在技术社区中的重要性，暗示该工具登上热门讨论榜单是理所当然的。
• [matcha-video] 推荐了另一个功能全面的浏览器内视频编辑器（https://wide.video），提供了FFmpeg之外的另一个选择。
• [guluarte] 推荐了ShellOracle工具，帮助不熟悉命令的用户自动生成命令。
• [bsenftner] 提出需要改进工具以处理包含空格的长文件名，特别是由AI视频模型生成的文件名。
• [danielvaughn] 表示自己在让LLM生成FFmpeg命令时遇到了困难，暗示实现类似功能并不简单。
• [raincole] 对浏览器中运行FFmpeg表示好奇，并询问是否通过WebAssembly实现。
• [somesun] 提供了另一个类似的FFmpeg在线工具（https://ffmpeg.app/）。
• [baobabKoodaa] 认为这是薄LLM包装器的一个完美用例。
• [p0w3n3d] 以幽默方式回应，表示无法执行操作。
• [pdyc] 分享了自己创建的视频编辑工具，通过可视化界面调整FFmpeg命令，旨在解决命令行操作困难的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：部分用户（如[danielvaughn]）在使用LLM生成FFmpeg命令时遇到问题，而其他用户（如[kkukshtel]、[toddmorey]）则认为这类工具非常有效。
• 技术细节：讨论中提到了文件名处理（[bsenftner]）、浏览器内运行FFmpeg的实现方式（[raincole]、[jjcm]）以及替代工具如Untrunc（[jjbinx007]）和ShellOracle（[guluarte]）。
• 资源分享：多个评论提供了额外的资源和工具链接，如Wide.video（[matcha-video]）、ShellOracle（[guluarte]）、FFmpeg.app（[somesun]）和自制的视频编辑工具（[pdyc]）。

data.title: James Webb, Hubble space telescopes face reduction in operations
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: NASA's Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes (JWST) face operational cuts due to budget limitations. Hubble's budget has remained flat for a decade, losing 30% of its purchasing power to inflation. The Trump administration's proposed 2026 budget aims to cut JWST's funding by 25%, from $187 million to $140 million, and Hubble's from $93.3 million to $85 million. These cuts may result in reduced telescope modes and less user support. JWST, still in its prime mission, may see a 25-35% reduction in science operations, affecting its 17 observation modes due to staff cuts. The budget shortfalls could decrease observation efficiency and limit available support for astronomers.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国政府对詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）及其他太空项目的预算削减，以及其背后的动机和影响。

不同观点：
• [devjab] 对预算削减感到困惑，尤其是不理解为何要削减太空项目的开支。他认为已经投入大量资金将设备送入太空，现在却不去充分利用，似乎是不合理的。他猜测是否是为了将部分工作外包给私营部门或有其他动机，甚至质疑是否与反科学政策有关。

• [jve] 指出詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜项目不仅仅涉及NASA，欧洲航天局（ESA）和加拿大航天局（CSA）也参与其中，因此质疑这些机构是否有机会接管部分操作。

• [derektank] 认为这种削减是短视的行为，指出为了节省占总预算极小部分的资金而放弃充分利用已经投入巨大的设备是不明智的。

• [spo81rty] 对运行望远镜需要300-400名员工表示质疑，作为纳税人，他想知道为什么需要这么多人力成本。

• [merman] 认为这些预算削减并不能直接证明当前政府是反科学的。他指出，拜登的2022财年预算估算与当前预算非常接近，因此不能单凭这些削减就断言是反科学。

• [october8140] 认为在政府不愿增加投入的情况下，可以考虑通过“出租”望远镜时间来解决资金问题，让富裕的机构支付费用使用。

• [bravesoul2] 简短地表示当前的混乱局面似乎是刻意而为。

• [jeisc] 以一种讽刺的方式表达了对太空防御能力的担忧，暗示如果外星人入侵，可能会因为削减预算而无法及时发现。

• [stogot] 对运行这些太空项目的昂贵预算感到不解，认为文章中提到的数字非常惊人。

补充讨论：
• 对太空项目预算削减的合理性存在争议，部分人认为这是短视行为，而另一些人则试图寻找替代方案，如将设备出租给私营机构。
• 对运行望远镜所需的人力成本以及整体预算的质疑和不解是另一个讨论焦点，显示出公众对高额预算支出的敏感性。
• 虽然有人质疑政府是否反科学，但也有观点指出不能仅凭预算削减就得出这样的结论，需要更多证据。

The James Webb Space Telescope is pictured here before being folded up for launch. Credit: NASA
Key Takeaways:
NASA's Hubble and James Webb telescopes face operational cuts due to budget limitations.
Reduced funding may lead to fewer available telescope modes and less user support.
Hubble's budget has remained flat for a decade, decreasing its purchasing power.
“It’s fewer people, really,” said Neill Reid.
Key takeaways sponsored by
The Space Store
See a mistake?
Contact us
.
The teams operating the Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) — NASA’s two most in-demand observatories and among its most scientifically productive missions — are preparing to reduce operations due to funding shortfalls, officials said last week at the summer meeting of the American Astronomical Society (AAS) in Anchorage, Alaska.
The comments came at a June 10 town hall held by the Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI), which is based in Baltimore, Maryland, and operates JWST and Hubble for NASA.
Speaking at the town hall, Neill Reid, multi-mission project scientist at STScI, said the institute is looking at a likely reduction of around 25 to 35 percent in science operations for JWST. The institute is also likely to reduce or drop support for several of Hubble’s instruments; they will still be available for observations, but the telescope’s staff will no longer be able to support them with regular calibration updates.
The threats to JWST and Hubble are due to a combination of factors, some of which have been brewing for years. Over the past year, NASA and STScI officials have warned of budgetary challenges and operational reductions due to flat budgets and inflation.
Another factor is funding cuts to both telescopes contained in the Trump administration’s budget proposal for 2026 — especially JWST, which would see its operating budget cut by 25 percent relative to planned 2024 operations, from $187 million to $140 million.
The cut to Hubble — down from $93.3 million in planned funds for 2024 to $85 million in 2026 — is less of a surprise. The Biden administration’s
2025 budget request
, which was never enacted, also contained a planned reduction in Hubble funding, down to $87.5 million in 2026. In 2024, NASA conducted
a review
of Hubble’s operations, seeking to reduce costs.
A
document
posted to NASA’s website May 30 says the Trump administration’s budget proposal “supports continued operations” of Hubble and JWST “at slightly reduced budget levels which assume operational efficiencies in FY 2026 and out.”
Budgetary issues
Speaking at the AAS town hall, STScI’s Neill Reid said Hubble’s budget has remained essentially flat over the past decade while inflation has increased, resulting in a drop in spending power of 30 percent. Any additional cuts to Hubble’s budget “will result in significant loss to science,” an STScI slide stated.
Part of the challenge facing Hubble, which launched in 1990, is that it “has lasted longer than people expected,” Reid told
Astronomy
. “NASA’s looking at how much money it has. And it’s trying to do as many things as possible. … If it were to build up the Hubble budget, it would be cutting something else.” STScI has made Hubble’s operation leaner, but eventually, the only way to save more money is to “stop doing things,” Reid said.
Unlike Hubble, JWST is still in the midst of its prime mission. The telescope, which cost $10 billion to construct, was launched in 2021 and began operations the following year. NASA originally hoped the telescope would operate for 10 years, but thanks to a highly accurate launch, there is enough fuel on board to last for more than 20 years.
Even if the Trump administration’s proposed budget cuts are rejected by Congress, JWST was already facing budgetary pressures. That’s partly because the observatory’s operations budget set by NASA in 2011 was idealistically low, said Reid.
“There was a sound amount of optimism that went into some of those, and there’s also been inflation,” said Reid. “So then you have the [presidential budget request] that comes in and cuts more. So we may be looking at reducing operations by 25 to 35 percent next year.”
Reid said STScI does not yet have a specific plan to deal with JWST’s budget shortfalls, but it will almost certainly involve reducing staff.
“It’s fewer people, really,” Neill Reid, multi-mission project scientist at STScI, told
Astronomy
. “[JWST has] got 17 different modes. Each of those modes needs people to support it, to calibrate it, to keep it going. So, if you cut the funding, you have fewer people. And you can’t ask people to do twice as much work. So what will happen is that there will be potentially fewer modes available. There will be less user support.”
It could also lead to less time spent taking observations, said Reid. “You may end up being much less efficient. There are fewer people to work on the scheduling. So you may not be able to put things together in the same way.” Overall, Reid said, “it’s

44521108.article_content:
'Chimpfluencers' Are Sticking Grass in Their Ears And Butts in Latest Viral Trend
Nature
10 July 2025
By
Michael Irving
Chimps have been seen following a bizarre new trend.
(Jake Brooker/Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust)
If chimpanzees had access to TikTok, the platform might soon be flooded with videos of 'chimpfluencers' wearing grass in their ears and butts – the latest trend going around a chimp sanctuary in Africa.
In August 2023, at the Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust sanctuary in Zambia, a trendsetting chimp named Juma was seen sticking a piece of grass into his ear, deep enough to stay there on its own. Within a week the fad went viral, as four other chimps in the group started copying his unusual accessory.
Not to be outdone, later that month Juma debuted a risqué variation: he inserted a blade of grass into his rectum, and left it dangling. This unorthodox trend also caught on, with five other chimps adopting the strange new fashion.
Related:
Bored Capuchin Monkeys Are Kidnapping Howler Babies in Weird New 'Trend'
The behavior fascinated researchers observing the captive chimpanzees (
Pan troglodytes
) . The grass didn't seem to serve a biological purpose – they weren't scratching itchy ears or butts, for example. Instead, the team hypothesizes that it might serve a social purpose.
"By copying someone else's behavior, you show that you notice and maybe even like that individual. So, it might help strengthen social bonds and create a sense of belonging within the group, just like it does in humans,"
says
Edwin van Leeuwen, biologist at Utrecht University in the Netherlands.
A chimp showing off its trendy new ear grass. (Jake Brooker/Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust)
Intriguingly, the event wasn't the first time Chimfunshi chimps had decorated their orifices with grass. An original trendsetter named Julie started the whole grass-in-ear thing way back in 2010, which caught on with seven other chimps. The behavior continues to this day among the group, even after Julie's death.
This seems to be a case of
social learning
and
cultural transmission
– after all, only one of the four groups observed back then exhibited the behavior, even though all lived in similar conditions. Weirdest of all is that more than a decade after Julie, Juma seems to have come up with the idea independently, since his group never had contact with hers.
The researchers suggest that fads with no clear purpose could be a holdover from the important ability to learn new
survival skills
. It's telling that wild chimps haven't been observed following 'useless' trends – only captive ones seem to have enough time on their hands.
"Chimpanzees can socially learn novel skills and primarily use them in contexts of personal interest, like nut-cracking and termite fishing," the researchers
write in a paper
about their observations.
"Yet, when selection pressures relax (e.g., due to systematic provisioning in captive care), chimpanzees may extend their social learning occasionally to behaviors without direct instrumental utility."
Non-functional
cultural trends
aren't unique to chimps either. In recent years, orcas have been seen
wearing dead salmon
on their heads like hats, and
sinking boats
in European waters – both of which seem to be fads.
A group of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (
Tursiops aduncus
) in South Australia started '
tail-walking
' along the surface of the water after one of them observed captive dolphins that had been trained to do the trick. Wild dolphins continued to perform the feat for decades afterwards, indicating the trend had been passed down culturally.
Studying animal cultures could help teach us more about our own. After all, is sticking grass in your butt really that different from
planking
or
eating laundry detergent pods
?
The research was published in the journal
Behaviour
.

data.title: A job queue in two lines of JavaScript
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了如何用两行JavaScript代码实现一个任务队列，确保任务按顺序执行。代码定义了一个`Job`类型和`enqueue`函数，利用Promise链处理任务的顺序，即使链中出现错误，任务依然会被执行。文章还提到，简单的`chain.then(job)`可能导致任务在链出错时不执行，因此建议使用`chain.then(job, job)`。此外，文章包含其他技术话题的简要提及和作者的一些个人观点与经历。文章末尾有作者的招聘广告和版权声明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Promise链的使用及其在不同场景下的有效性和适用性，包括内存管理、错误处理、代码风格以及在生产环境中的应用。

不同观点：
• **lerp-io** 认为，每次调用`enqueue()`都会创建一个新的promise，并引用前一个promise，这会导致promise链不断增长，造成垃圾回收压力。

• **ameliaquining** 提出，可以使用`chain.finally(job)`来代替`chain.then(job, job)`，因为浏览器已经支持这个API超过七年，这样写更符合习惯。

• **Inviz** 指出，这种promise链的方式在高吞吐量的情况下不合适，会产生垃圾回收压力，但在普通情况下是有效的。

• **theThree** 给出了一个示例代码，使用`async`和`await`来处理任务队列，避免显式使用promise链。

• **cluckindan** 补充，如果需要在失败时记录日志，需要在`catch`中处理，否则日志需要由任务本身记录。

• **egorfine** 质疑提到的代码是否属于JavaScript，暗示可能涉及TypeScript或其他语言。

• **vivzkestrel** 认为，生产级别的应用需要更健壮的机制，比如BullMQ，而不是简单的promise链。

• **neals** 请求对代码进行详细解释，表明对代码理解有困难。

• **90s_dev** 分享了自己的经验，提到曾使用类似的技巧处理一个可能是竞态条件的chrome API，但最终还是删除了这部分代码，不过仍然对当时的解决方案感到自豪。

• **gabrielsroka** 指出，提到的代码是TypeScript，而不是JavaScript。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种实现方式，包括使用`finally`方法、`async/await`语法、以及生产环境下的健壮机制如BullMQ。
• 错误处理也是一个讨论重点，特别是如何在promise链中有效记录错误日志。
• 语言的区分也被提及，特别是TypeScript和JavaScript之间的区别。
• 最后，不同开发者的实际经验分享也为讨论增加了一些实用背景和个人见解。

data.title: Myanmar’s proliferating scam centers
data.author: WaitWaitWha
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了缅甸东部诈骗中心的迅速扩张，即使在今年2月的大规模打击行动后，这些犯罪窝点仍在继续建设。通过分析卫星图像和目击者证词，日经新闻揭示了这些“边境监狱”的规模和持久性。KK Park是其中最大的诈骗中心之一，无人机照片显示了拘留设施和工作区域。一名南亚男子称在那里被强迫参与恋爱诈骗，每天工作16小时，生活条件恶劣，暴力频繁。卫星图像还显示，其他诈骗窝点在缅甸-泰国边境涌现，许多外国人被贩运至此从事欺诈活动。尽管进行了打击，至少16个可疑诈骗点仍在运作，其中8个仍在建设中。这些设施具有严密监控、大规模容纳能力以及沿河而建等特点，主要用于控制和强迫外国人实施诈骗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：东南亚诈骗活动及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **关于参与者的国籍和动机**  
  - otikik认为文章过于侧重日本视角，而忽视了中国在事件中的角色，例如中国投资者、中文视频平台和标识等，表明中国的影响力更大。  
  - 30minAdayHN指出，一些人参与诈骗是为了薪水，而非自愿参与，这与印度的电话诈骗中心类似。  
  - apwell23提到许多来自印度喀拉拉邦的人被卷入这些骗局，批评印度政府没有采取足够措施解救被绑架公民。

• **关于诈骗活动的发展趋势**  
  - 55555预测，随着AI技术的发展，诈骗将变得更加复杂和难以防范，例如通过AI克隆声音进行电话诈骗。  
  - kragen提出疑问，是否AI最终会取代人类在这些诈骗活动中的角色。  
  - booleandilemma提到一部中国电影《No More Bets》反映了这一问题，尽管电影中的国家未明确指出是缅甸。

• **关于诈骗活动的地点和组织形式**  
  - dddddaviddddd引用维基百科的“全球有组织犯罪指数”，指出缅甸在犯罪活动方面排名高于哥伦比亚和墨西哥。  
  - jacknews补充，除了大规模的诈骗中心，还有许多较小的中心分布在公寓楼和办公楼中，特别是在柬埔寨。

• **关于应对措施和国际影响**  
  - gkanai建议日本将打击诈骗中心作为对缅甸官方发展援助的条件。  
  - jjani质疑为何不通过关闭Starlink来切断诈骗中心的通信，因为这些地点是众所周知的。  
  - throwaway48476认为，只有确保所有国际交易可逆，才能有效遏制诈骗。

• **关于个人安全和风险**  
  - tonyhart7警告，诈骗团伙不仅在缅甸活动，还会绑架邻国的公民，建议独自旅行者要保持警惕。

补充讨论：
• **关于纪录片和揭露**  
  - charlysl分享了一个纪录片链接，其中一些管理人员甚至公开了诈骗中心的运作情况。  
  - rft提到在CCC会议上有关诈骗中心的生活揭露，特别是从缅甸逃出来的人提供的文件和信息。

争议焦点：
• 针对不同国家在诈骗活动中扮演的角色和责任存在争议，例如中国和日本的影响力问题。  
• 关于AI在未来诈骗活动中可能发挥的作用存在不同看法。

Myanmar
Myanmar
Myanmar
Source:

Read in Japanese
Visual Investigation
These borderland 'prisons' have three common features
July 11, 2025
The number of scam centers in eastern Myanmar is expanding at a rapid pace. Even after a large-scale crackdown in February, construction has continued -- underscoring that criminal hubs have not been eradicated. Nikkei analyzed satellite imagery and eyewitness testimony to reveal the scale and persistence of the crisis.
A drone photograph of KK Park, one of the largest scam centers, shows the dormitory and work area where the escapee says he was detained.
Inside,
that one is like
a prison
A man from South Asia who says he was held for six months at KK Park -- one of the largest scam centers -- recounts his experience. He was forced to engage in romance scams, tricking victims into paying money by making them believe they were in a romantic relationship. He lived with seven others in a cramped room and worked 16 hours a day.
A satellite image of KK Park is shown.
Violence was commonplace. According to the South Asian man's testimony, a supervisor struck him with a boot. One other worker was dragged to a torture room and beaten so severely he could no longer stand.
A set of 16 satellite images illustrates the locations of KK Park and other suspected scam centers. The first view shows that the sites were empty lots before becoming scam center sites.
Other criminal compounds have emerged along the Myanmar-Thailand border. By cross-referencing satellite photos with official records and interviewing experts, Nikkei identified suspected scam bases in and around Myawaddy, Kayin state.
The sequence of photos transitions to images of the same locations after the compounds were constructed, highlighting the rapid pace of development that began accelerating in the second half of the 2010s.
In the second half of the 2010s, Chinese-backed companies began developing casino complexes in the region. When the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the casino industry, many of these facilities were converted into hubs for online fraud.
A map of the Myawaddy area in eastern Myanmar. Clusters of suspected scam centers line the border with Thailand.
The proliferation has not slowed. At least 16 suspected scam sites have been documented, and construction was ongoing at eight of them even after the crackdown earlier this year.
According to numerous reports, large numbers of foreign nationals are trafficked into these compounds and forced to
perpetrate scams.
Japan has been affected. In February 2025, a Japanese high school student believed to have been held captive in Myanmar was rescued and later arrested on fraud charges.
According to Myanmar's military government, from October 2023 to June 2025, authorities deported more than 66,000
foreign nationals who had stayed in the country illegally to participate in fraud or gambling.
Satellite images of Huanya Park -- which was raided earlier this year -- show that the red roof of a massive building is nearing completion. The images are from March and May.

"All but one of the compounds seems to be operating as normal [after the crackdown]," said Eric Heintz, a global analyst at International Justice Mission, a U.S.-based nongovernmental organization that supports people who have escaped scam centers.

for monitoring workers

Layouts designed for monitoring workers
The first feature is a layout designed to allow for the close surveillance of workers. The expansive grounds are surrounded by fences and walls, lined with numerous structures believed to be watchtowers. Nikkei analyzed and mapped the positions of the structures by using satellite imagery and social media posts.
Source: Douyin account @美岐不是美岐 (Meiqi Bushi Meiqi) (Nikkei added a white frame)
A video posted on the Chinese video-sharing platform Douyin shows elevated platforms towering above the surrounding walls. Satellite imagery also captured the main roofed gate on the compound's south side.
"It is quite common that the cameras are pointing inside and the wire along the wall bends inside," said Mark Bo of the nonprofit EOS Collective, which researches online scam operations. "It is not to keep people out of the compound. It is to keep people inside the compound."

data.title: Burning a Magnesium NeXT Cube (1993)
data.author: leoapagano
data.article_summary: 本文简要描述了作者计划燃烧一个NeXT立方电脑外壳的过程。NeXT立方电脑由铸镁制成，这种材料坚固轻便，但成本高。作者自高中起对镁燃烧的特性感兴趣，一直想燃烧NeXT立方外壳。1991年，作者通过NeXT的硬件副总裁Rich Page获得了一个空镁壳，但因各种原因未立即实施燃烧实验。随着NeXT可能停产立方电脑、转向"NeXT Brick"的传闻，作者计划用燃烧立方照片作为杂志封面，象征其终结。在NeXT正式宣布停产硬件后，作者与编辑Dan Ruby决定在地下室进行燃烧实验，并拍摄照片。文章提到获取燃烧工具和选择燃烧地点的细节，但未详述实验结果。照片已上传至Flickr。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于燃烧镁及相关实验、技术与历史的讨论

不同观点：
• [alnwlsn] 描述了燃烧汽车废弃发动机中的镁块的实际经验，详细介绍了燃烧过程和注意事项，并强调不要模仿这种危险行为。该评论提供了具体的操作步骤和潜在的危险，如镁与水的反应。
• [maxbond] 对评论的写作风格表示了 nostalgia，认为这种过度详细的风格在十几年前更为常见，并指出现在的网络写作更加简练，同时对过去的写作风格表示欣赏。
• [shrubble] 引用了过去摄影师使用镁燃烧来调整曝光的技术细节，强调了这种方法在过去的摄影中很常见。
• [WillAdams] 表达了对过去技术设备的怀念，如NeXT Cube电脑，并提到了对当前技术继承与发展的不满，如GNUstep和Altsys Virtuoso软件。
• [mproud] 认为评论中的故事可能曾在其他媒体如Wired或Hacker News上出现过，表明这种内容在过去已经被讨论过。
• [HPsquared] 提到了汽车中使用镁组件增加了消防员的危险，指出了镁在实际应用中的安全隐患。
• [pantalaimon] 对文章缺少图片表示失望，尽管文章讨论了燃烧镁的摄影。
• [ethan_smith] 提供了技术背景，指出NeXT Cube使用镁外壳的原因及其极高的燃烧温度，强调了这种材料的危险性。
• [donatj] 分享了儿时对镁燃烧特性的经验，并对镁燃烧难以扑灭的特点表示担忧，质疑其在实际应用中的安全性。
• [chasil] 讨论了NeXT公司选择处理器架构的历史，认为如果选择了不同的处理器，公司硬件的命运可能会有所不同。
• [sim7c00] 对文章的叙述方式表示困惑，特别是在叙述视角上的转换，但同时也表示对燃烧实验的兴趣和幽默感。
• [cat_plus_plus] 分享了自己燃烧食物制作视频的爱好，并通过食物燃烧的难易程度讨论了食物的营养成分和安全性。
• [a3w] 和 [lo_zamoyski] 都提到了对缺少备份或实验设备图片的失望，认为文章缺少视觉资料。
• [tucnak] 认为文章冗长乏味，尤其是其中大段描述打电话的内容，表明对文章的叙事风格不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：燃烧镁实验的危险性与趣味性。部分评论者如[alnwlsn]和[donatj]强调了实验的危险，而[sim7c00]和[cat_plus_plus]则表达了对这种实验的兴趣和幽默感。
• 技术背景：如[ethan_smith]和[chasil]提供了关于NeXT Cube技术细节和历史背景的信息，丰富了讨论的技术深度。
• 风格与叙述：如[maxbond]和[tucnak]对文章的写作风格和叙事方式提出了不同的看法，反映了读者对文章可读性和长度的关注。

44523372.article_content:
Note: We have recently posted
all
the photos
from the cube burning on Flickr.
Date:
Wed, 24 Mar 93 19:11:02 EST
From:
simsong
To:
druby
Subject:
cube burning
Cc:
edit
To:
Dan Ruby, Editor,
NeXTWORLD Magazine
From:
Simson L.
Garfinkel, Senior Editor, NeXTWORLD Magazine
Subject: NeXTCube Serial Number AA001032
Date:
March 16, 1993
Dear Dan,
I am writing this
memo to explain what happened to the case our NeXTCube Computer, Serial Number
AA001032.
As you know, years
ago, when NeXT first contemplated making computers, Steve Jobs decided that
machines should be in the shape of a cube, and that they should be built from
cast magnesium.
Although magnesium is a
relatively expensive metal, it is remarkably strong and lightweight.
No doubt, this let NeXT save on shipping
expenses, although the added handling and manufacturing costs was one of the
factors which led to the cube's high cost.
At the time that NeXT brought their system to market, the only other
company to incorporate a magnesium case was Grid, which was making a portable
computer.
(I am told that Apple also
uses magnesium for the inside case of its Duo computers, but I haven't been
able to verify this fact.)
As a former chemist,
I was attracted to the NeXT's magnesium case for a different reason: magnesium
burns with a brilliant white flame.
When I was in high school, I used to steal magnesium metal from the
chemistry lab and set it on fire in my backyard.
A two-inch long strip would burn for nearly a minute, the
white-hot flame slowly turning the shiny grey metal into a plume of white smoke
(magnesium oxide --- a harmless material which is the main ingredient in milk
of magnesia.)
When NeXT announced
that the first NeXT Cube was made of cast magnesium, I am sure that I was not
the only person who imagined what fun could be had by setting it ablaze.
Of course, at more than seven thousand
dollars each, I doubted that anybody would ever actually carry out the
experiment.
Anyway, during the
fall of 1991, I interviewed Rich Page, NeXT's then vice-president for hardware,
for an article which we later ran in NeXTWORLD Extra.
At the time, I asked Mr. Page if he could get me an empty NeXT
Cube case for the purpose of having such a burning.
Page smiled and said that he thought something could be
arranged.
A few days later, he called
me up and said that I could pick up an empty cube at NeXT's Freemont factory.
My plan was to light
the cube along its top edge.
I imagined
that the magnesium would burn brightly and the fire would move slowly down the
sides, a triumphant expression of the power of NeXT's technology to set the
world afire.
I drove down to
Freemont the next day and picked up the cube, which was waiting for me behind
behind the receptionist desk at the factory.
Page had delivered exactly what I had asked for --- an empty magnesium
case, without any electronics, back plane, or rubber feet.
The case was also missing the NeXT logo, but
you can't get everything.
I put it in
the back of my Jeep and drove back to my apartment in Berkeley.
Over the next few
months, I tried to think of some way to ignite the magnesium.
One idea that I had was to use a mixture of
potassium permaganate and glycerin, which bursts into flames and produces an
enormous amount of heat after just a few minutes.
I asked a chemist friend if he could supply me with the
ingredients: he suggested that I simply use a MAP gas torch.
"It's hotter and easier to
control," he said.
Unfortunately,
I left California before I was able to carry out the experiment.
I left the cube with my friend Sophia for
safe keeping.
A year later, Sophia
told me that she was sick of keeping the cube.
I came out to California and transferred the cube from Sophia's house to
your basement.
By this time, we had
started to hear rumors that NeXT might be discontinuing its cube in favor of
the "NeXT Brick," a RISC-based computer.
I started thinking that we might want to use a photograph of the
burning cube for the cover of that issue that announced the NeXT Cube's
demise.

data.title: Telefónica DE shifts VMware support to Spinnaker due to cost
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: Telefónica德国公司因VMware支持续费价格过高，选择将支持服务转给Spinnaker。在Broadcom收购VMware后，取消了永久许可证，并要求客户转向订阅套餐，导致续费报价是原先的五倍。 Telefónica主要使用vSphere 8.0和7.0，认为VMware提供的完整云平台套件过于昂贵且 unnecessary。公司此前三年已支付约500至800万欧元，无法接受新报价。虽然已使用Spinnaker支持Oracle软件，但仍进行了市场对比，最终决定转至Spinnaker以节省成本。尽管不打算立即离开VMware，但计划在2026年底前逐步退出。同时，类似的情况也发生在北卡罗来纳州立大学，该校放弃了VMware和Nutanix，选择了Red Hat的虚拟化解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Broadcom收购VMWare后的影响以及相关技术决策的合理性

不同观点：
• ygritte认为，Broadcom严重破坏了VMWare的产品。个人用户不再有合适的产品可使用，企业云业务也在流失客户。
• Havoc质疑Broadcom是否故意通过一次性的回报来破坏VMWare的品牌声誉。
• ojosilva将Broadcom的行为比作Computer Associates，认为Broadcom在模仿其压榨企业客户的策略，尤其是在续约费用方面。

补充讨论：
• ahofmann对文章中关于德国电信公司的描述提出质疑，指出德国实际上只有三家主要移动服务提供商，文章的描述虽然技术上正确但具有误导性。
• trebligdivad对Spinnaker如何在没有许可证的情况下提供安全支持感到困惑，质疑其合法性和技术实现方式。
• znpy对文章整体表达不满，认为文章没有清晰解释Spinnaker与VMWare的关系，以及Telefonica是否正在从虚拟化转向云部署，并对Broadcom的普遍反感表示认同。

争议焦点：
• Broadcom是否故意通过破坏VMWare品牌来获得短期经济利益（Havoc的观点与其他评论者对Broadcom策略的批评相关）。
• Spinnaker在没有许可证的情况下如何合法且有效地提供安全支持（trebligdivad的质疑与其他技术细节的澄清需求相关）。
• 文章对技术细节和市场动态的描述是否准确且易于理解（ahofmann和znpy对文章内容的准确性和清晰性提出质疑）。

44557757.article_content:
Virtualization
23
Telefónica Germany offloads VMware support to Spinnaker due to high renewal costs
23
'Our offer from Broadcom was five times higher than we expected'
Dan Robinson
Fri 11 Jul 2025
//
11:32 UTC
The German arm of telecoms biz Telefónica has shifted support for its VMware installed base to Spinnaker after Broadcom quoted it a renewal figure five times the size of what it was previously paying.
Telefónica Germany made the switch to Spinnaker at the start of the year when its existing support with VMware, now a subsidiary of silicon-and-software giant Broadcom, expired.
VMware must support crucial Dutch govt agency as it migrates off the platform, judge rules
READ MORE
The telco was running vSphere, largely on perpetual licenses it had purchased previously, with regularly renewed agreements to cover maintenance and other support.
However, as
Reg
readers will be aware, Broadcom decided to end perpetual licenses after it bought VMware, and has sought to move customers to
subscription packages
covering both software and support.
These bundle together multiple pieces of software, typified by VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), which includes vSphere, vSAN, NSX and other components to provide a complete private cloud platform. The result is often a far higher price tag than customers paid before.
"Our offer from Broadcom was five times higher than we expected," Holger Berndt, Professional Lead for Software Asset Management at Telefónica told
The Register
.
"We told them that we don't use all parts of the VCF. They offered us the whole solution, and it was very good, and it's a lot of things that we don't need, that was the main problem," he added.
Telefónica currently uses only vSphere 8.0 and 7.0, so the full-blown VCF suite is considered somewhat overkill for its requirements.
"They told us we are a valued customer, then they offered us a price it was, let me think, five times higher than expected. And that was not acceptable, because we had paid approximately €5 to €8 million over three years already, and so you can figure out what they offer[ed] us," Berndt said.
It seems Broadcom was not prepared to be flexible on licensing in order to keep the telco, one of Germany's largest, as a customer. VMware
previously indicated
it believes users will come to realize the value of what's on offer, if they would just use more of everything that is included in the subscription package.
VMware’s rivals ramp up their efforts to create alternative stacks
How Broadcom is quietly plotting a takeover of the AI infrastructure market
The SmartNIC revolution fell flat, but AI might change that
VMware and Siemens spar over where to stage software licence showdown
That price rise came as a shock, especially to Telefónica's management, but the timing was good because Broadcom approached the firm about licensing in August, according to Berndt, and so Telefónica knew it had until the end of the year when its maintenance would expire to do something about it.
University quits VMware, then quits Nutanix too
North Carolina State University has quit VMware, and Nutanix, and settled on Red Hat for its virtualization needs.
Red Hat revealed the university's virtualization odyssey in a Monday
post
in which Security Applications team IT Manager Shawn Taylor revealed that after Broadcom acquired VMware, he adopted virtualization contender Nutanix.
Taylor told Red Hat: "It didn't get us anywhere. We just replaced one expensive thing with another."
He's now moving to Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization and plans to use it for VMs, containers, and will add OpenShift Data Foundation for storage too.
– Simon Sharwood
At this stage, Telefónica had already been using Spinnaker for a couple of years to provide support for the Oracle software it operates, so the biz was an obvious choice, although Berndt says Telefónica did its due diligence and compared what it was offering against rivals.
The process threw up one minor hurdle: Telefónica was running some subscription-based software, for which it acquired a secondhand perpetual licence so that it didn't have to prolong any contracts with VMware.
Berndt claims his company is actually saving money from moving support to Spinnaker. It's clear that he is less than happy with Broadcom over this whole matter.
"We never thought to go away from VMware until Broadcom [came] up with this new solution, and we are not angry with Broadcom, but it's not acceptable. It's not acceptable what they're doing at the moment, that they tell you that you are the one of the valuable customers, and then they do this," he said.
Now, Telefónica has an exit program, but it will take time to follow this through, as the department is still in the process of preparing a request for quotation (RFQ) to go out to potential bidders.
"The earliest we move away from VMware will be the end of '26 something like that," Berndt told us. "It's a lot of planning, it's a lot of calculating, budget wise, and so on, so it was not the easiest

data.title: Impacts of adding PV solar system to internal combustion engine vehicles
data.author: red369
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在汽车上安装太阳能板的实用性和效益

不同观点：
• **janosch_123**：自己制造电动汽车并计算过太阳能车顶的效益。由于车顶弧形和转换损耗（需要升压到400V才能充电），在高峰时段最多只能获得500W的电力，增加了很多复杂性但收益有限。
• **Veliladon**：虽然太阳能车顶有一定道理，但在不理想的环境下，能量回报率（EROEI）很难超过1。将太阳能板安装在房屋或建筑物的屋顶上会更有效果。
• **londons_explore**：太阳能车顶的一个主要好处是可以防止汽车长时间不使用时电池耗尽，一个小型的书本大小的太阳能板就足够应对。
• **jollyllama**：传统内燃机车（ICE）和混合动力车之间有区别。对于通常停在户外的车辆，太阳能板可以作为解决电池耗尽的临时方案。
• **infecto**：认为这个问题早已解决，复杂性和风阻损失使得太阳能车顶几乎没有意义，固定太阳能装置会更好。
• **Qem**：提出大型卡车可能是一个值得考虑的领域，因为卡车车顶面积大，且货运是难以脱碳的领域。还可以通过调整行驶时间来增加太阳能利用。
• **throwaway3b03**：提到在ecomodder社区中，移除交流发电机是一个常见做法，可以减少复杂性和发动机负荷，提高燃油效率。
• **vondur**：建议使用小型电池为车辆在炎热天气下的通风系统供电。
• **torginus**：引用了一位瑞典人的例子，他通过在混合动力车上安装2块太阳能板，实现了日常通勤不用充电。
• **condensedcrab**：提到Aptera车型，即使设计为超轻量级，也只能通过车顶太阳能恢复10%的电池电量，提醒工程选择有时受制于当前的监管环境。
• **lenerdenator**：建议在车内安装太阳能充电的空调系统，可以减少怠速时间。
• **testing22321**：分享了一对夫妇通过携带的太阳能板为电动车提供动力，完成了穿越西非的旅行。
• **jwr**：认为即使太阳能车顶从工程角度有意义，心理上的接受度可能是更大的问题，因为很多人对电动车的抵触情绪强烈。
• **ianbooker**：提到20年前太阳能车顶通风系统就已经存在。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的实际案例和实验（如Aptera车型、瑞典人的混合动力车）提供了具体的例子和数据。
• 心理接受度和文化抵触被认为是推广太阳能车顶的一个重要障碍。
• 不同的应用场景（如大型卡车、电动车长途旅行）可能为太阳能车顶提供更多的实际效益。

data.title: Concurrent Programming with Harmony
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文档介绍了并发编程及Harmony虚拟机的相关内容。主要涵盖了并发编程的基础概念、问题（如非确定性和非原子性）、关键区段、锁的实现与使用、条件变量、死锁与饥饿问题、 actors模型与消息传递、屏障同步、以及分布式共识算法等主题。附录部分提供了Harmony语言参考、模块说明、虚拟机细节及简化语法等技术细节。文档通过大量代码示例和图表解释了并发程序的设计、测试与调试方法，并探讨了如Paxos等高级分布式算法。

主要讨论点：并发事件是否能够被充分理解和控制

• [fuzzfactor] 认为人们无法充分了解并发事件，因为它们无时无刻不在发生，无论人们是否愿意面对。这暗示了并发事件的复杂性和不可避免性。

补充讨论：
• [fuzzfactor] 的观点似乎基于并发事件的普遍性和不确定性，但没有提出具体的例子或解决方案。
• 该评论没有涉及是否可以通过技术或方法来更好地理解或管理并发事件，留下了进一步讨论的空间。
• 潜在的争议焦点在于是否能够通过学习和实践有效掌握并发事件的处理，还是只能被动接受其复杂性。

data.title: Interview with Google's Android leader Sameer Samat
data.author: gbil
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了作者与谷歌Android生态系统总裁Sameer Samat的对话。Samat对作者使用MacBook和Apple设备感到好奇，因为他正在推动Chrome OS和Android的整合，并希望了解人们如何使用笔记本电脑。Samat还介绍了Android 16的新特性，包括对平板支持、更流畅的动画和高度定制化，目标是打造现代且用户友好的体验。此外，谷歌改进了Android的发布流程，使其更频繁地更新，并通过“Android Drops”功能实现无需操作系统更新的体验提升。关于Android与iOS的选择，Samat认为切换不应有障碍，用户应能无缝迁移数据和应用程序。
